title: Interior Design for Dwarka Expressway's Luxury Towers: Godrej, Puri & Sobha Compared

excerpt: Godrej, Puri and Sobha towers on Dwarka Expressway differ in size, handover spec and interior brief. Compare Godrej Meridien, Puri Emerald Bay, Sobha City and Sobha Altus, with what each needs and what it costs.
keyTakeaways: Most of These Towers Are Premium, Not Ultra-Luxury — Godrej Meridien, Puri Emerald Bay and Sobha City are about 1,400–3,000 sq ft; Sobha Altus is the top tier at 3,000–4,000+ sq ft.
Handover Spec Sets the Budget Split — What the developer provides decides how much goes into fixing basics versus adding design.
Don't Rip Out What Works — A developer's modular kitchen or engineered stone floor may only need upgrading, not replacing.
Plan Around the Builder's Services — AC provisions, kitchen exhaust points and electrical layouts are fixed; working with them keeps costs down.
Sobha Altus Needs a Fuller Brief — Bespoke joinery, architectural lighting, integrated automation and curated furniture rather than mainly wardrobes and a kitchen.

contentHtml:
Godrej Meridien (Sector 106), Puri Emerald Bay (Sector 104) and Sobha City (Sector 108) are premium towers with 2BHK to 4BHK homes of roughly 1,400 to 3,000 sq ft, handed over with tiled floors, basic bathrooms and, in some cases, a modular kitchen. Interiors here focus on storage, kitchens, lighting and false ceilings rather than a full rebuild. Sobha Altus (Sector 106) is the corridor's top tier, with 3BHK and 4BHK homes of about 3,000 to 4,000+ sq ft starting around ₹6.66 crore, and calls for a fuller luxury brief.

Dwarka Expressway has moved from "upcoming corridor" to one of Gurgaon's most active luxury addresses, and three developer names come up again and again: Godrej, Puri and Sobha. Their towers differ in size, handover specification and the kind of interior brief they produce. This guide compares them, from Godrej Meridien and Puri Emerald Bay to Sobha City and the newer Sobha Altus, and explains how interior design for Dwarka Expressway's luxury towers changes from one to the next.

The towers at a glance

ProjectSectorHomesSizesAsking priceStatus

Sobha City108About 1,452 in 9 towers, ~39 acres2BHK to 4BHK; 1,381 to 2,963 sq ftAbout ₹3.2 to ₹7 crore (~₹23,000 per sq ft)Ready; later phases ongoing

Figures are from listing portals and RERA references and vary by source and tower. Always confirm sizes from your own sale documents.

What each developer hands over, and what it means for design

The handover specification decides how much of the interior budget goes into fixing basics versus adding design.

ProjectTypical handoverWhat the interior brief usually covers
Godrej MeridienVitrified tile floors, oil-bound distemper walls, standard bathroom fittings, aluminium sliding windowsWardrobes, modular kitchen, false ceilings and lighting, wall finishes, often a bedroom floor upgrade
Puri Emerald BayLaminated wood floor in the master bedroom, vitrified tiles elsewhere, acrylic emulsion walls, modular kitchen with hob and chimneyWardrobes, kitchen upgrade or reconfiguration, lighting, feature walls, furniture
Sobha CityVitrified tiles (natural or engineered stone in some towers), laminated timber in the master bedroom, AC provision, tiled kitchen with sinkModular kitchen, wardrobes, false ceilings, lighting, AC, furniture
Sobha AltusMarketed with Italian marble flooring and floor-to-ceiling windows; confirm the final handover listA full luxury brief: bespoke joinery, lighting design, automation, curated furniture

Two practical points follow:

  • Do not rip out what works. A modular kitchen or engineered stone floor from the developer may only need upgrading, not replacing.
  • Plan around services. AC provisions, kitchen exhaust points and electrical layouts were fixed by the builder. Working with them keeps the cost down.

Godrej Meridien: making a premium plan feel bespoke

Godrej Meridien's 2BHK to 4BHK homes are efficient, well-proportioned layouts with plenty of greenery around the towers. Interiors here are about personalising a standard plan:

  • Full-height wardrobes to make the most of compact bedrooms.
  • A fitted modular kitchen, often L-shaped or parallel depending on the plan.
  • False ceilings with layered lighting in the living and dining areas.
  • Floor upgrades in bedrooms, where many owners replace vitrified tile with wood-look finishes.
  • Balconies as outdoor rooms with seating, planters and lighting.

Puri Emerald Bay: upgrading a well-specified handover

Puri Emerald Bay arrives better finished than many corridor projects, with a modular kitchen and wood flooring in the master bedroom. The brief is more about upgrading than building:

  • Kitchen upgrades: new shutters, countertop, hardware, or reconfiguration. A kitchen with a centre island, for example, suits homes where the layout allows.
  • Statement living rooms: feature walls, panelling and a stronger lighting plan.
  • Matching wardrobes and joinery throughout, so the developer's finishes and the new work feel like one design.

Sobha City: designing for Sobha's build quality

Sobha is known for its in-house construction quality, and Sobha City's larger 3BHK and 4BHK homes give room for a more complete brief:

  • Open-plan living and dining, connecting the main rooms around one design language.
  • Modular kitchens built from scratch, since the kitchen is handed over as a tiled room with a sink.
  • AC and false ceilings planned together, using the builder's AC provisions.
  • Domestic help rooms in some towers, which change how storage and the utility area are planned.

Sobha Altus: the corridor's ultra-luxury tier

Sobha Altus sits at a different level: fewer homes, larger 3BHK and 4BHK units of about 3,000 to over 4,000 sq ft, and a starting price around ₹6.66 crore. A brief here looks more like a Golf Course Road project:

  • Bespoke joinery made to the room, rather than modular systems throughout.
  • Lighting designed as architecture, making the most of floor-to-ceiling glazing.
  • Integrated automation for lighting, climate, curtains and security, planned before ceilings.
  • Curated furniture and art, with long-lead imported pieces ordered early.

For how this kind of brief differs, see what makes Golf Course Road interiors different.

For size-by-size budgets, see our interior design cost guide for 2BHK, 3BHK and 4BHK homes in Gurgaon and our comparison of 3BHK vs 4BHK interiors on Dwarka Expressway.

Planning interiors around possession

  • Start design before the keys arrive. Measurements from the builder's plan, confirmed on site at possession, let work begin immediately.
  • Inspect the handover. Note tile defects, seepage and electrical issues in writing to the builder before interior work starts.
  • Check society rules: work hours, lift use, debris removal and deposits.
  • Fix the kitchen exhaust and AC routes early; they decide ceiling and kitchen layouts.

Our Dwarka Expressway possession planning guide covers the full timeline, and our modular kitchen guide by Dwarka Expressway floor plan covers kitchens.

Our work in these towers

The Omega Group is headquartered on Dwarka Expressway, and our portfolio includes homes in all three developers' projects on the corridor:

  • Godrej Meridien, Tower 3, Sector 106
  • Puri Emerald Bay, Sector 104: a modular kitchen with a traditional wood finish and a centre island
  • Sobha, Sector 108: an apartment interior with open-plan living and dining

One team handles design, procurement and site execution, with 70+ quality checks on a typical project and 90% of projects completed on schedule. Book a free consultation and bring your floor plan, or see our interior design services on Dwarka Expressway.

faqs.question: Which are the luxury towers on Dwarka Expressway?
faqs.answer: Well-known premium and luxury projects include Godrej Meridien (Sector 106), Puri Emerald Bay (Sector 104) and Sobha City (Sector 108). Sobha Altus (Sector 106) is a newer, higher tier, with 3BHK and 4BHK homes of about 3,000 to over 4,000 sq ft.

faqs.question: How big are apartments in Godrej Meridien, Puri Emerald Bay and Sobha City?
faqs.answer: Listings show Godrej Meridien at about 1,366 to 2,720 sq ft carpet area, Puri Emerald Bay at about 1,550 to 2,450 sq ft, and Sobha City at about 1,381 to 2,963 sq ft. Figures vary by source and tower, so confirm from your sale documents.

faqs.question: What do these projects provide at handover?
faqs.answer: Godrej Meridien is listed with vitrified tiles and basic fittings. Puri Emerald Bay adds a modular kitchen and wood flooring in the master bedroom. Sobha City includes AC provisions and wood flooring in the master bedroom, with a tiled kitchen. Always check the handover list for your tower.

faqs.question: How is interior design different for Sobha Altus?
faqs.answer: Sobha Altus homes are larger and priced higher, so the brief is closer to an ultra-luxury project: bespoke joinery, architectural lighting, integrated automation and curated furniture, rather than mainly wardrobes and a modular kitchen.

faqs.question: How much does interior design cost for a Dwarka Expressway apartment?
faqs.answer: Full-home turnkey interiors with The Omega Group start at ₹15 lakh+, scaling with size and specification. Larger luxury homes are usually planned per sq ft, with Gurgaon luxury work typically at ₹2,500 to ₹8,000+ per sq ft.

faqs.question: Should I replace the developer's modular kitchen or flooring?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. If the kitchen carcass and flooring are in good condition, upgrading shutters, countertops, hardware or finishes is usually better value than replacing everything.

faqs.question: Has The Omega Group worked in these towers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our portfolio includes homes in Godrej Meridien Tower 3 (Sector 106), Puri Emerald Bay (Sector 104) and a Sobha project in Sector 108, and our studio is on Dwarka Expressway.
